parse.title: O Love That Will Not Let Me Go

wikitext.*:
{{versions
| title = O Love That Will Not Let Me Go
| author = George Matheson
| notes = "Dr. Matheson says this hymn was 'written in the Manse of my former parish (Innellan, Argyleshire) one summer evening in 1882. It was composed with extreme rapidity; it seemed to me that its construction occupied only a few minutes, and I felt myself rather in the position of one who was being dictated to than of an original artist I was suffering from extreme mental distress, and the hymn was the fruit of pain.' [L. MSS.] This hymn first appeared in the [[Portal:Church of Scotland|Church of Scotland]] magazine, ''[[Life and Work]]'', in 1883. From thence it passed into the ''[[Scottish Hymnal]]'' 1884; and there set to special music by Dr. [[Author:Albert Lister Peace|A. L. Peace]]. It is a beautiful and tender hymn and worthy of extensive use." —{{DoH link|O Love that wilt not let me go}}.
}}
